biography.plain_text: Grzegorz Przondziono is a Polish retail executive who led Agata through its expansion into a national furniture chain. Based in Katowice, the business grew under the ownership of the Ćwik family. His presidency spanned more than two decades, encompassing new store openings and a widening range of furnishings and decorative accessories.

confidence.reason: Contemporaneous executive reporting and the later statutory exit support the historical tenure. Company materials establish the national furnishings business; family ownership is independently described.

biography.html: Grzegorz Przondziono is a Polish retail executive who led Agata through its expansion into a national furniture chain. Based in Katowice, the business grew under the ownership of the Ćwik family. His presidency spanned more than two decades, encompassing new store openings and a widening range of furnishings and decorative accessories.

long_biography.plain_text:
The remodelling of Agata’s furniture store in Gliwice in 2014 set a pattern for Grzegorz Przondziono’s approach to its showrooms. New and refurbished shops adopted a consistent design, while a premium area in Warsaw brought Italian furniture brands to customers seeking more expensive pieces.

During the pandemic, Przondziono joined the Polish heads of IKEA and JYSK in seeking permission to reopen furniture stores. Their appeal argued that customers needed furnishings for working and studying at home. Under his presidency, Agata’s board also committed company funds to medical equipment and protective supplies for Poland’s health services.

confidence.reason: His quoted retail strategy supports the showroom material. The jointly signed appeal and the company's own funding announcement support the public decisions, with corporate action and funds clearly attributed.
